QF.id: AIF Valuation Taxation and Good Practices_11

answer.text: Estimates exit value at a future date and discounts back at a high target return

explanation.text: The Logic: The VC method first estimates the terminal value of the business at the expected exit. That terminal value is then discounted back to its present value using the estimated hurdle or target return rate. The required ownership stake is derived from the investment amount relative to that present value, with an adjustment for expected future dilution. The Trap: Only using historical statements, valuing the start-up at zero, or relying purely on P/E multiples each miss the forward-looking exit-and-discount mechanic that defines the VC method. Note: Based on NISM Series XIX-A workbook pages 249-251, which describe the VC method's terminal value at exit, present-value discounting at the hurdle rate, target ownership calculation, and dilution adjustment.
